title: Personnel of the Hampton band
summary: Monk names the trumpets, trombones, reeds and rhythm section, including Art Farmer, Quincy Jones, Clifford Brown, Jimmy Cleveland, Benny Golson and Philly Joe Jones.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: But back to what the musicians in the band...and he had quite a few good, top people in the band during the period I was there. Just to name some of the personnel: in the trumpet section it was Art Farmer, there was Quincy Jones, there was Al Williams, there was The Whistler. There were changes come along a little later, like Clifford Brown, Benny Bailey. And also Emory -- gosh, I can't think of Emory's -- big, fat trumpet player. I can't think of his name, but we used to call him the Fat Boy because he was huge, maybe 300 pounds in weight. Then another guy by the name of Davenport, I believe, were some of turnover people in the trumpet section.

The trombone section was Jimmy Cleveland, Buster Cooper and Al -- oh, I'm sorry, I can't think of that trombone player's name (Hayes). And the rhythm section -- the reed section was Bobby Plater, he was beautiful, Bobby Plater; Morris Lane, Clifford Solomon, Oscar Estelle, the baritone, and...who else am I missing? It's been a lot of years and I keep...I've got up to the date in my mind.

Anyhow, the rhythm section was Elmer Gill, piano player, and I later worked with him for a spell, and after Elmer, me playing bass and William Mackell playing guitar. And after Elmer, Hamp went without piano. The band...
...working without a piano, he used to play the vibes. But that's what the band consisted of. Benny Golson played with us for a while. Pardon?
He didn't have an organ player during that period?

No, there was no organ. But we had periods where... there was a short period Benny Golson worked, and a short period Philly Joe Jones played drums. Who else came in and out of the band, just short periods where they did a segment of the thing? Papa Jo Jones played some, a couple of gigs.
